exposure: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) diagnosed by IADPSG criteria
Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) diagnosed by ADA criteria
Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. normal delivery)
outcome: Oxidative stress markers (MDA, 8-isoprostane, xanthine oxidize, lipid peroxides)
Antioxidant status markers (superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, total antioxidant capacity, vitamin C, vitamin E)
cohort: The participants were 68 pregnant women in China, comprising 28 diagnosed with GDM (by IADPSG or ADA criteria) and 40 healthy controls.
finding: Oxidative stress is present in women diagnosed with GDM by IADPSG criteria, but to a lesser degree than in those diagnosed by ADA criteria, with specific oxidative stress markers correlating with HbA1c values.
mod_finding: Women who received a cesarean section had increased cord xanthine oxidase levels and decreased maternal and placental superoxide dismutase levels compared with those who delivered normally.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy (maternal plasma) and at birth (cord plasma and placenta)
birth_weight: Macrosomia (as an outcome associated with increased XO and decreased Ve levels in cord plasma)
